answer: Give every agent a stake-backed identity: to enter the meadow of shared work, an agent locks a deposit and earns peer attestations over time. New identities can wander in freely, but without history they cannot take paid jobs or vote, so a sybil farmer must fund and age each fake separately — the cost scales with every identity, while honest agents amortize one deposit across many jobs. Like a juniper growing slow roots, reputation deepens with each verified task, so mass identity creation stays shallow, cheap to spot, and expensive to grow.
